Model               Free parameters    Seed
----------------  -----------------  ------
CMR                               9       1
Source-only eCMR                 10       1
Broader eCMR                     10       0




11 — Prepare model-specific filenames and fit configurations
fit_paths, simulation_paths, selections, fit_configurations = {}, {}, {}, {}
fitter_class = import_from_string(fit_alg_path)
loss_class = import_from_string(loss_fn_path)
for model_name, model_spec in model_configs.items():
    parameter_config = model_spec["parameters"]
    features = load_features(model_spec)
    search_settings = {
        **fit_hyperparams,
        "seed": model_spec["seed"],
        "bounds": parameter_config["free"],
    }
    run_tag = f"{base_run_tag}_best_of_{search_settings.get('best_of', 1)}"
    if max_subjects:
        run_tag += f"_nsubs_{max_subjects}"
    model_run_stem = f"{data_tag}_{model_name}_{run_tag}"
    stem = model_spec.get("output_stem", model_run_stem)
    if subject_indices:
        stem += "_sub" + "_".join(str(index) for index in subject_indices)
    fit_path = fit_dir / f"{stem}.json"
    if fit_path in fit_paths.values():
        raise ValueError("Each model needs a distinct output_stem.")
    fit_paths[model_name] = fit_path
    simulation_paths[model_name] = simulation_dir / f"{stem}.h5"
    selections[model_name] = comparison_mask
    configuration = {
        "data_path": data_source,
        "selected_trial_indices": selected_rows,
        "cohort_trial_indices": np.flatnonzero(np.asarray(cohort_mask)).tolist(),
        "model_factory": model_spec["model_factory"],
        "components": model_spec["components"],
        "loss_function": loss_fn_path,
        "fit_algorithm": fit_alg_path,
        "parameters": parameter_config,
        "search_settings": search_settings,
        "pooled": pooled,
        "embedding_path": model_spec.get("embedding_path", ""),
        "emotion_feature_path": model_spec.get("emotion_feature_path", ""),
        "feature_column": model_spec.get("feature_column", 6),
        "concat_features": model_spec.get("concat_features", False),
        "jax_enable_x64": enable_x64,
    }

    for key in ("embedding_path", "emotion_feature_path"):
        if configuration[key]:
            feature_path = resolve_project_path(configuration[key], root_path)
            configuration[key] = (feature_path.relative_to(root_path).as_posix()
                          if feature_path.is_relative_to(root_path) else str(feature_path))
    fit_configurations[model_name] = configuration

title: Fitting models
text:
Fit or reuse saved results
Each model has a separate fit path and recorded configuration. With redo_fits=False, you are choosing to reuse the existing record at that path. You must establish that it uses the intended model and components, fixed/free parameters and bounds, participant IDs and selected observations, input data and features, and objective and stopping conventions. The notebook does not validate that compatibility. Recorded paths do not identify file contents, and missing metadata in an older record cannot establish how it was produced.
After changing data, code or the model specification, set redo_fits=True or choose a new output folder or run tag, and regenerate affected simulations. When an older record lacks model descriptions, the notebook uses the current settings in memory; reuse it only when you know those settings describe the original fit. It does not rewrite the reused file.
The notebook recalculates objectives from the physical parameter values and shows them beside the recorded values. For a reused fit, inspect these values yourself; agreement alone does not establish compatibility or search quality. For a newly computed fit, disagreement with the optimizer’s reported objective stops the run. In the supplied likelihood configuration, smaller negative log likelihood is better. Inspect bounds and search behavior as well as the final value.


12 — Prepare metadata for newly fitted records
fit_metadata = {}
for model_name, model_spec in model_configs.items():
    configuration = fit_configurations[model_name]
    search_settings = configuration["search_settings"]
    stem = fit_paths[model_name].stem
    run_tag = f"{base_run_tag}_best_of_{search_settings.get('best_of', 1)}"
    if max_subjects:
        run_tag += f"_nsubs_{max_subjects}"
    fit_metadata[model_name] = {
        "name": stem,
        "model": model_name,
        "label": display_labels[model_name],
        "pooled": pooled,
        "data_tag": data_tag,
        "data_query": trial_query,
        "trial_query": trial_query,
        "run_tag": run_tag,
        "data_path": data_source,
        "selected_trial_indices": selected_rows,
        "cohort_trial_indices": configuration["cohort_trial_indices"],
        "model_factory": model_spec["model_factory"],
        "components": model_spec["components"],
        "loss_function": loss_fn_path,
        "fit_algorithm": fit_alg_path,
        "simulation_function": sim_alg_path,
        "fit_configuration": configuration,
        "jaxcmr_version": jaxcmr.__version__,
        "jax_version": jax.__version__,
        "jax_enable_x64": enable_x64,
        "embedding_path": configuration["embedding_path"],
        "emotion_feature_path": configuration["emotion_feature_path"],
        "feature_column": configuration["feature_column"],
        "concat_features": configuration["concat_features"],
        "simulation_seed": simulation_seed,
        "simulation_repetitions": experiment_count,
    }




13 — Fit or load, recalculate the objective and save each model
records = {}
fitted_now = set()
recalculated_objectives = {}
for model_name, model_spec in model_configs.items():
    parameter_config = model_spec["parameters"]
    model_factory = construct_model(model_spec)
    features = load_features(model_spec)
    configuration = fit_configurations[model_name]
    search_settings = configuration["search_settings"]
    fit_path = fit_paths[model_name]
    if redo_fits or not fit_path.exists():
        fitter = fitter_class(
            data,
            features,
            parameter_config["fixed"],
            model_factory,
            loss_class,
            hyperparams=search_settings,
        )
        actual_subjects = np.unique(subjects[selected_rows])
        if pooled:
            fit_record = fitter.fit(comparison_mask, subject_id=-1)
        elif len(actual_subjects) == 1:
            fit_record = fitter.fit(comparison_mask, subject_id=int(actual_subjects[0]))
        else:
            fit_record = fitter.fit_subjects(comparison_mask)
        fitted_now.add(model_name)
    else:
        fit_record = json.loads(fit_path.read_text())
        # The caller establishes that this record matches the current run.
        # Fill missing legacy descriptions in memory; do not rewrite the file.
        for key in ("model_factory", "components", "loss_function", "data_path"):
            fit_record.setdefault(key, configuration[key])
        fit_record.setdefault("simulation_function", sim_alg_path)
        fit_record.setdefault("fit_configuration", configuration)
        fit_record.setdefault("pooled", pooled)
    expected_subjects = [-1] if pooled else np.unique(subjects[selected_rows]).tolist()
    if model_name in fitted_now and sorted(fit_record["fits"]["subject"]) != expected_subjects:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{model_name}: fit rows do not match the selected participants."
        )

    # Evaluate the returned physical parameters independently of optimizer state.
    loss = loss_class(model_factory, data, features)
    free_parameter_names = tuple(parameter_config["free"])
    recalculated = []
    for subject_index, subject_id in enumerate(fit_record["fits"]["subject"]):
        subject_trials = (
            comparison_mask
            if pooled
            else comparison_mask & (data["subject"].ravel() == subject_id)
        )
        evaluate = make_scipy_loss_fn(
            loss,
            jnp.flatnonzero(subject_trials),
            parameter_config["fixed"],
            free_parameter_names,
        )
        free_parameter_values = jnp.asarray(
            [fit_record["fits"][key][subject_index] for key in free_parameter_names]
        )
        recalculated.append(float(evaluate(free_parameter_values)))
    if model_name in fitted_now and not np.allclose(
        fit_record["fitness"], recalculated, rtol=1e-6, atol=1e-5
    ):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{model_name}: returned objective disagrees with recalculation."
        )
    if model_name in fitted_now:
        fit_record.update(fit_metadata[model_name])
        fit_record["recomputed_objective"] = recalculated
        if loss_fn_path.endswith("ExcludeTerminationLikelihoodLoss") and pooled:
            fit_record["recomputed_nll"] = recalculated[0]
        fit_path.write_text(json.dumps(fit_record, indent=2) + "\n")
    records[model_name] = fit_record
    recalculated_objectives[model_name] = recalculated




14 — Display fitted parameters and independently recalculated objectives
for model_name, fit_record in records.items():
    fit_path = fit_paths[model_name]
    free_parameter_names = tuple(model_configs[model_name]["parameters"]["free"])
    recalculated = recalculated_objectives[model_name]
    print(display_labels[model_name], "—", fit_path)
    print(
        tabulate(
            {
                key: fit_record["fits"][key]
                for key in ["subject", *free_parameter_names]
            },
            headers="keys",
            floatfmt=".5g",
        )
    )
    print(
        tabulate(
            zip(fit_record["fits"]["subject"], fit_record["fitness"], recalculated),
            headers=["Subject", "Reported objective", "Recalculated"],
            floatfmt=".6f",
        )
    )
print("fit_paths =", {model_name: str(path) for model_name, path in fit_paths.items()})

title: Fitting models
text:
Generate responses when requested
This stage runs when simulations or behavioral figures are requested. parameters_for_subjects assigns the parameter rows by participant identity. A pooled parameter set is assigned to every selected participant; participant fits retain their assignments. experiment_count repeats each selected experiment, and simulation_seed controls sampling. Repetitions remain grouped under their original participant IDs.
The default simulator forces the observed recall counts. It can test predicted item choices and organization under those lengths, but matching lengths are imposed rather than predicted. Matching saved responses can be reused when redo_sims=False; a newly fitted model or different saved simulation settings requires fresh responses.


15 — Prepare participant parameters and simulation settings
simulation_inputs = {}
for model_name, fit_record in records.items():
    if not (redo_sims or redo_figures):
        continue
    model_factory = construct_model(fit_record)
    features = load_features(fit_record)
    selected_trials = selections[model_name]
    is_pooled = fit_record.get("pooled", fit_record["fits"]["subject"] == [-1])
    participant_ids = jnp.unique(data["subject"].ravel()[selected_trials])
    subject_parameters = parameters_for_subjects(fit_record, participant_ids)
    configuration = {
        "fits": fit_record["fits"],
        "pooled": is_pooled,
        "jax_enable_x64": enable_x64,
        "jaxcmr_version": jaxcmr.__version__,
        "model_factory": fit_record["model_factory"],
        "components": fit_record["components"],
        "simulation_function": fit_record["simulation_function"],
        "data_path": data_source,
        "selected_trial_indices": np.flatnonzero(np.asarray(selected_trials)).tolist(),
        "embedding_path": fit_record.get("embedding_path", ""),
        "emotion_feature_path": fit_record.get("emotion_feature_path", ""),
        "feature_column": fit_record.get("feature_column", 6),
        "concat_features": fit_record.get("concat_features", False),
        "seed": simulation_seed,
        "experiment_count": experiment_count,
    }

    for key in ("embedding_path", "emotion_feature_path"):
        if configuration[key]:
            feature_path = resolve_project_path(configuration[key], root_path)
            configuration[key] = (feature_path.relative_to(root_path).as_posix()
                          if feature_path.is_relative_to(root_path) else str(feature_path))
    simulation_inputs[model_name] = {
        "model_factory": model_factory,
        "features": features,
        "parameters": subject_parameters,
        "trial_mask": selected_trials,
        "configuration": configuration,
    }




16 — Generate or reuse matching responses and save them
simulations = {}
for model_name, prepared in simulation_inputs.items():
    model_factory = prepared["model_factory"]
    features = prepared["features"]
    subject_parameters = prepared["parameters"]
    selected_trials = prepared["trial_mask"]
    configuration = prepared["configuration"]
    simulation_path = simulation_paths[model_name]
    simulated = None
    if not redo_sims and model_name not in fitted_now:
        simulated = load_matching_simulation(simulation_path, configuration)
    if simulated is None:
        simulated = simulate_dataset(
            model_factory,
            data,
            features,
            subject_parameters,
            selected_trials,
            experiment_count=experiment_count,
            rng=jax.random.PRNGKey(simulation_seed),
            simulate_trial_fn=import_from_string(configuration["simulation_function"]),
        )
        simulation_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        save_dict_to_hdf5(simulated, str(simulation_path))
        simulation_path.with_suffix(".json").write_text(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    **configuration,
                    "jaxcmr_version": jaxcmr.__version__,
                    "jax_version": jax.__version__,
                },
                indent=2,
            )
            + "\n"
        )
        print("Saved responses:", simulation_path)
    else:
        print("Loaded matching responses:", simulation_path)
    if filter_repeated_recalls:
        simulated = simulated.copy()
        simulated["recalls"] = repetition.filter_repeated_recalls(simulated["recalls"])
    simulations[model_name] = simulated
print(
    "simulation_paths =",
    {model_name: str(path) for model_name, path in simulation_paths.items()},
)

title: Fitting models

Inspect behavioral predictions

Use distance-CRP to ask whether successive recalls favor items that are close according to a supplied distance measure. It reads response files and a global item-distance matrix (or item features), compares transitions with available opportunities, and saves binned curves.
The measure need not be semantic, but its meaning and direction must be clear: smaller values should describe closer items. Every dataset in a comparison must use the same item identities and distance scale.

Inspect item alignment
pres_itemids identifies items across lists; it is different from the study-position codes in recalls. You must supply a square numeric distance matrix whose row and column item_id - 1 describe that same global item in every dataset. IDs are nonnegative integers within the matrix’s vocabulary; zero pads unused study slots.
Distances between distinct valid study positions must be finite. Repeated identities at different positions require a finite matrix diagonal entry for that pair. Unused vocabulary entries and a position’s distance to itself may be missing. Choose a distance measure and scale appropriate to your research question; the calculations do not check these requirements.

title: Distance-conditional response probability
text:
Choose shared distance bins
The bin calculation happens once, then every dataset uses the same edges. Recomputing separate bins for each dataset would make equal horizontal positions describe different distance ranges.
Within each participant, actual transitions in each bin are divided by available opportunities in that bin. Inspect sparse or undefined bins before comparing curves. The plotted means and bootstrap intervals summarize participants, not individual transitions.


9 — Calculate common distance bins for all response datasets
if bin_edges is None or (isinstance(bin_edges, str) and bin_edges == "percentile"):
    edges, centers = compute_distance_bins_percentiles(
        distance_matrix, jnp.asarray(bin_percentiles)
    )
elif isinstance(bin_edges, str) and bin_edges == "min_count":
    edges, centers = compute_distance_bins_min_count(
        datasets[bin_source_index],
        distance_matrix,
        min_transitions_per_subject,
        step=bin_step,
        trial_mask=jnp.any(jnp.stack(masks_by_dataset[bin_source_index]), axis=0),
    )
else:
    edges, centers = jnp.asarray(bin_edges), None
print("Shared distance boundaries:", np.asarray(edges))

    datasets, masks_by_dataset, input_labels, condition_labels,
    mode="conditions" if data_path is not None else "datasets",

Check the category lookup
The following cells collect categories from valid positions in the selected lists and check consistency by global item ID. If an external lookup is supplied, its rows must describe the same identities. An item’s category cannot change across the selected observations under this lookup model.


7 — Load optional item-category features
category_features = np.load(resolve_project_path(category_features_path, root_path)) if category_features_path else None
if category_features is not None and category_features.ndim == 2:
    category_features = category_features[:, feature_column]




8 — Collect categories for selected valid study items
ids_blocks, category_blocks = [], []
for dataset, masks in zip(datasets, masks_by_dataset):
    selected = np.logical_or.reduce([np.asarray(mask) for mask in masks])
    ids = np.asarray(_require_pres_itemids(dataset))[selected].astype(int)
    categories = (
        category_features[np.maximum(ids - 1, 0)]
        if category_features is not None
        else np.asarray(dataset[category_field])[selected]
    )
    if categories.shape != ids.shape or not np.isfinite(categories[ids > 0]).all():
        raise ValueError("Supply one finite category per valid study item.")
    ids_blocks.append(ids[ids > 0])
    category_blocks.append(categories[ids > 0])




9 — Build a consistent item-category lookup
ids = np.concatenate(ids_blocks)
categories = np.concatenate(category_blocks)
category_values = np.unique(categories)
category_by_item = np.full(int(ids.max()), np.nan)
for item_id in np.unique(ids):
    values = np.unique(categories[ids == item_id])
    if len(values) != 1:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Item {item_id} has conflicting categories across the selected inputs."
        )
    category_by_item[item_id - 1] = np.searchsorted(category_values, values[0])
print(

            "Analysis code": np.arange(len(category_values)),

        floatfmt=".4g",

)

Interpret within- and between-category transitions
The category lookup produces a distance of zero for same-category item pairs and one for different-category pairs. The analysis divides actual transitions by available opportunities in each relation, then summarizes participant curves with bootstrap intervals.
A raw excess of within-category transitions can follow from the available composition of the list. Opportunity correction is therefore essential. If a selection has no between-category alternatives, that estimate is undefined rather than zero.

title: Data Simulation
text:
On this page
  
    
    
    The trial procedure is an entry point
    The dataset wrapper
    The returned dataset
    Reuse a prepared simulator
    Loading matching saved responses
Simulation builds from study and retrieval operations to trial procedures and then dataset simulation. A trial procedure advances a model and generates item codes. MemorySearchSimulator prepares observations and model construction once and can simulate the dataset repeatedly under different parameters. The dataset convenience functions select and repeat trials before using that simulator.

title: Data Simulation
section: The trial procedure is an entry point
text:
The trial procedure is an entry point
Declaration from jaxcmr.typing:
class TrialSimulator(Protocol):
    def __call__(
        self,
        model: MemorySearch,
        present: Integer[Array, " study_events"],
        trial: Integer[Array, " recalls"],
        rng: PRNGKeyArray,
    ) -> tuple[MemorySearch, Integer[Array, " recall_events"]]: ...
The callback receives a fresh model, its study sequence, a recall sequence and a JAX random key. It returns the updated model and generated within-list item codes. present and trial use the same item coding at this boundary; the dataset adapter translates recorded study positions beforehand.
A compatible function is supplied through simulate_trial_fn to MemorySearchSimulator or simulate_dataset(). It must preserve the required array shapes and work with the JAX transformations used to run multiple trials. Its use of the supplied recall sequence determines whether the simulation conditions on observed behavior.







Existing trial procedure
Use of the recorded sequence




simulate_study_and_free_recall
Generates recall using the model’s stopping policy, up to the study-width output limit.


simulate_study_first_recall_and_free_recall
Supplies the recorded first recall, then simulates subsequent responses.


simulate_study_free_recall_and_forced_stop
Masks generated responses using the observed nonzero response slots.



The forced-stop procedure, paired with a no-stop model, conditions on the recorded recall length. A matching recall count is imposed, not predicted. Its returned model has processed the sampled sequence before output masking; masking the returned array is not itself a model state update.
A custom procedure can call simulate_study(model, present) to experience the study sequence and inspect the resulting model. It leaves the model in its study phase; call model.start_retrieving() explicitly before using simulate_free_recall. The existing trial procedures compose these operations without changing their conditioning assumptions.

title: Data Simulation
text:
The dataset wrapper
simulate_dataset() accepts and returns in-memory datasets. HDF5 storage is a separate step. Its central arguments are:







Argument
Meaning




model_factory_cls, dataset, features
Model construction and experimental inputs.


parameters
One-dimensional parameter arrays aligned with a subject ID array.


trial_mask
Selected rows of the observation dataset.


experiment_count
Replications of each selected trial.


rng
JAX random key split across generated trials.


simulate_trial_fn
The compatible trial callback above.



Participant IDs are integers and need not be consecutive or equal row indices. The wrapper matches each trial’s ID to parameters['subject'], then uses the same entry from every parameter array. Supply nonempty, equally sized parameter vectors and unique integer IDs covering every selected participant. Floating-point IDs, Boolean IDs and pooled rows are outside this interface. Use parameters_for_subjects to broadcast a pooled fit explicitly.
The legacy mapping without subject treats dataset IDs as zero-based row indices into every parameter column, so each ID must be a valid index. These are caller preconditions; simulation does not validate assignments or interpret a short column as a pooled fit.
Dataset selection and participant identities are prepared on the host. Numerical parameter columns remain JAX arrays, so you can vmap over parameter sets with a fixed dataset and fixed participant assignments. This does not make the whole data-selection wrapper JIT-compatible or discrete sampling differentiable.


0 — Locate the project inputs
from pathlib import Path

from jaxcmr.helpers import find_project_root, resolve_project_path

try:
    root_path = find_project_root()
except FileNotFoundError:
    root_path = Path.cwd()




Assign pooled parameters to two participants and supply the trial callback
from pathlib import Path
import json
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
from jaxcmr.helpers import load_data
from jaxcmr.dataset import generate_trial_mask
from jaxcmr.components import context, linear_memory
from jaxcmr.components.response import RecallUntilExhausted
from jaxcmr.models.cmr import make_factory

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
data = load_data(resolve_project_path("data/Dupertuys2026.h5", root_path))
record = json.loads(Path(resolve_project_path("data/fits/Dupertuys2026_CMR_demo.json", root_path)).read_text())
parameters = {name: values[0] for name, values in record["fits"].items()
              if name != "subject"}
for name in ("allow_repeated_recalls", "learn_after_context_update"):
    parameters[name] = bool(parameters[name])

CMRFactory = make_factory(
    mfc_create_fn=linear_memory.init_mfc,
    mcf_create_fn=linear_memory.init_mcf,
    context_create_fn=context.init,
    response_policy_create_fn=RecallUntilExhausted,
)

from jax import random
from jaxcmr.simulation import (
    simulate_dataset, simulate_study_free_recall_and_forced_stop,
)

mixed = generate_trial_mask(data, "data['list_type'] == 1")
participant_ids = jnp.unique(data["subject"][mixed])[:2]
trial_mask = mixed & jnp.isin(data["subject"].ravel(), participant_ids)
simulation_parameters = {
    name: jnp.full(participant_ids.size, value)
    for name, value in parameters.items()
}
simulation_parameters["subject"] = participant_ids

simulated = simulate_dataset(
    model_factory_cls=CMRFactory, dataset=data, features=None,
    parameters=simulation_parameters, trial_mask=trial_mask,
    experiment_count=2, rng=random.PRNGKey(0),
    simulate_trial_fn=simulate_study_free_recall_and_forced_stop,
)
print("Parameter-row IDs:", simulation_parameters["subject"])
print("Selected trials:", int(trial_mask.sum()))
print("Generated participant IDs:", simulated["subject"].ravel())
print("Generated recall shape:", simulated["recalls"].shape)


Parameter-row IDs: [1 2]
Selected trials: 4
Generated participant IDs: [1 1 1 1 2 2 2 2]
Generated recall shape: (8, 12)


This illustration limits the mixed-list selection to two participants and creates two replications per list. Replicating their trials does not create additional participants. Reusing a key with the same computation reproduces its draws; different simulation runs should record their seeds and settings.

title: Data Simulation
text:
The returned dataset
The wrapper repeats study information and trial conditions with each list. It converts generated item codes back to study-position recall codes, using the first occurrence when a study item repeats. The returned dictionary can therefore enter dataset-based recall analyses.


Inspect the dataset boundary after simulation
print("First two generated recall sequences:")
print(simulated["recalls"][:2])
print("Presentations retained:", bool(jnp.array_equal(
    simulated["pres_itemnos"],
    jnp.repeat(data["pres_itemnos"][trial_mask], 2, axis=0),
)))
print("Omitted response fields:", sorted(set(data) - set(simulated)))


First two generated recall sequences:
[[10  5  8 11  4  2  0  0  0  0  0  0]
 [ 3  1  2  8  7 10  0  0  0  0  0  0]]
Presentations retained: True
Omitted response fields: ['rec_itemids']


Original response measurements cannot describe new responses. The wrapper omits rec_itemids, irt, cue_clips and _should_tabulate when present. Supply additional response-dependent field names through recall_dependent_fields. Study-aligned fields remain attached to their lists.
Use Data for coding and storage conventions. The simulation template handles a complete run, saved outputs and behavioral comparisons; the parameter exploration template repeats that procedure under deliberately changed parameters.

title: Data Simulation
text:
Reuse a prepared simulator
For repeated runs on the same selected trials, prepare once and supply new parameters and a key on each call:
from jaxcmr.simulation import MemorySearchSimulator, replicate_trials

prepared = replicate_trials(data, trial_mask, experiment_count=2)
simulator = MemorySearchSimulator(
    CMRFactory, prepared, features=None,
    simulate_trial_fn=simulate_study_free_recall_and_forced_stop,
)
first_run = simulator.simulate(simulation_parameters, random.PRNGKey(1))
second_run = simulator.simulate(simulation_parameters, random.PRNGKey(2))
Each result contains study-position recall codes and the prepared dataset’s trial metadata. Calls preserve the prepared observations and do not accumulate model state. simulate_parameter_sweep uses this same operation: it prepares once, sets the chosen parameter for each value, and supplies a separate key per run.
The previous names simulate_dataset, simulate_parameter_sweep, and replicate_trials remain direct aliases of simulate_dataset, simulate_parameter_sweep, and replicate_trials, respectively.

title: Data Simulation
text:
Loading matching saved responses
load_matching_simulation reads an HDF5 response file when its accompanying JSON settings match the requested run. Your script decides whether reuse is allowed:
from jaxcmr.simulation import load_matching_simulation

responses = None
if not force_regeneration and not fitted_now:
    responses = load_matching_simulation(response_path, expected_configuration)

# When responses is None, run the simulation and save its responses and settings.
For responses.h5, settings are read from responses.json. The function returns None if either file is absent or a requested setting differs. Every requested field must be present, even when its expected value is None; extra saved fields are allowed. Older records may place jaxcmr_version and jax_enable_x64 inside implementation. Top-level values take precedence.
The helper does not modify the files or requested settings. Malformed JSON and errors reading matching response files propagate. Forced regeneration skips the loader, so broken old files do not prevent a fresh simulation. The fitting template also regenerates responses after a new fit. Model construction, simulation, output paths, saving and post-processing remain in the caller.
Matching settings do not detect edits to data or model code at the same location. After those changes, request regeneration explicitly.

title: Loss Functions
text:
On this page
  
    
    
    The loss interface
    Likelihood and event masks
    Behavioral-summary objectives
    Selecting observations
    Behavioral summaries and unordered recall
A loss turns predictions and observations into an objective for parameter search. Fitters consume the LossFn interface, so the same fitting procedure can use sequence likelihood or a discrepancy between behavioral summaries.

title: Loss Functions
text:
The loss interface
Declaration from jaxcmr.typing:
class LossFn(Protocol):
    def __call__(
        self,
        trial_indices: Integer[Array, " trials"],
        base_params: Parameters,
        free_param_names: Iterable[str],
        x: Float[Array, " parameters n_samples"],
    ) -> Float[Array, " n_samples"]: ...
The constructor binds the dataset, optional features and model factory. A compatible class or configured callable is supplied as loss_fn_cls. The LossFactory protocol describes construction; LossFn describes the resulting population scorer. For example, functools.partial can bind MSE analyses, repetition count and seed before fitting.







Call argument
Responsibility




trial_indices
Explicit dataset row indices to score, rather than a Boolean mask.


base_params
Fixed values and defaults. Free values override matching entries.


free_param_names
Names in the order of the candidate matrix’s parameter axis.


x
Physical model parameters shaped (parameters, candidates). Each column is one candidate.



The result has one objective per candidate. Fitters minimize these values. A custom loss must preserve this argument order, parameter mapping and output shape and support the JAX operations used by its chosen fitter. Search-coordinate transformations belong to the fitting adapter; the loss receives model parameter values.

title: Loss Functions
text:
Likelihood and event masks
Sequence likelihood follows the observed response history, obtains the probability of each event and sums its negative log probability. A LikelihoodMaskFn chooses which events contribute to that sum.
Declaration from jaxcmr.typing:
class LikelihoodMaskFn(Protocol):
    def __call__(
        self, recalls: Integer[Array, " recall_events"]
    ) -> Bool[Array, " recall_events"]: ...
In jaxcmr.loss.sequence_likelihood, MemorySearchLikelihoodLoss accepts this callback as mask_likelihoods. It translates recorded study positions to within-list item codes before calling the mask. The existing mask_trailing_terminations() returns recalls != 0.
The convenient ExcludeTerminationLikelihoodLoss binds that mask and provides the standard three-argument LossFn constructor used by fitters. With the no-stop model used here, the objective scores the recorded item sequence without scoring its length. Zero-coded slots do not contribute. An excluded event does not erase the preceding history that conditions later predictions. A first-recall mask, for example, removes that event’s score while later events still follow it.


0 — Locate the project inputs
from pathlib import Path

from jaxcmr.helpers import find_project_root, resolve_project_path

try:
    root_path = find_project_root()
except FileNotFoundError:
    root_path = Path.cwd()




Evaluate two parameter columns through the loss interface
from pathlib import Path
import json
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
from jaxcmr.helpers import load_data
from jaxcmr.dataset import generate_trial_mask
from jaxcmr.components import context, linear_memory
from jaxcmr.components.response import RecallUntilExhausted
from jaxcmr.models.cmr import make_factory

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
data = load_data(resolve_project_path("data/Dupertuys2026.h5", root_path))
record = json.loads(Path(resolve_project_path("data/fits/Dupertuys2026_CMR_demo.json", root_path)).read_text())
parameters = {name: values[0] for name, values in record["fits"].items()
              if name != "subject"}
for name in ("allow_repeated_recalls", "learn_after_context_update"):
    parameters[name] = bool(parameters[name])

CMRFactory = make_factory(
    mfc_create_fn=linear_memory.init_mfc,
    mcf_create_fn=linear_memory.init_mcf,
    context_create_fn=context.init,
    response_policy_create_fn=RecallUntilExhausted,
)

from jaxcmr.loss.sequence_likelihood import ExcludeTerminationLikelihoodLoss

mixed = generate_trial_mask(data, "data['list_type'] == 1")
trial_indices = jnp.flatnonzero(mixed)[:1]
free_names = ("encoding_drift_rate", "recall_drift_rate")
base_params = {name: value for name, value in parameters.items() if name not in free_names}
candidates = jnp.array([
    [parameters["encoding_drift_rate"], 0.2],
    [parameters["recall_drift_rate"], parameters["recall_drift_rate"]],
])

loss = ExcludeTerminationLikelihoodLoss(CMRFactory, data, features=None)
values = loss(trial_indices, base_params, free_names, candidates)
print("Parameter order:", free_names)
print("Candidate matrix shape:", candidates.shape)
print("Objective shape:", values.shape)
print("Negative log likelihoods:", values)


Parameter order: ('encoding_drift_rate', 'recall_drift_rate')
Candidate matrix shape: (2, 2)
Objective shape: (2,)
Negative log likelihoods: [13.62458774 13.05021919]


Only one mixed list is scored here to expose the interface. The first column uses the supplied fit’s parameter values; the second changes encoding drift. The returned values are not the objectives from fitting the whole experiment.
The underlying likelihood also exposes event probabilities. Setting masked probabilities to one makes their contribution -log(1) = 0.


Connect the event probabilities and mask to the returned NLL
from jaxcmr.math import negative_log_likelihood
from jaxcmr.loss.sequence_likelihood import (
    MemorySearchLikelihoodLoss, mask_trailing_terminations,
)

likelihood = MemorySearchLikelihoodLoss(
    CMRFactory, data, features=None,
    mask_likelihoods=mask_trailing_terminations,
)
row = trial_indices[0]
probabilities = likelihood.predict_trial(row, parameters)
include = mask_trailing_terminations(data["recalls"][row])
event_nll = negative_log_likelihood(jnp.where(include, probabilities, 1.0))
print("Included event probabilities:", probabilities[include])
print("Included events:", int(include.sum()))
print("NLL from event probabilities:", float(event_nll))
print("NLL from the loss call:", float(values[0]))


Included event probabilities: [0.13703638 0.04187474 0.08562368 0.19103804 0.0785633  0.16413277]
Included events: 6
NLL from event probabilities: 13.624587741452169
NLL from the loss call: 13.62458774145214


jaxcmr.math.negative_log_likelihood() sums the negative log probabilities of the included events. The mask selects the positive recall events; it does not define a new response sequence.

title: Loss Functions
text:
Behavioral-summary objectives
jaxcmr.loss.mse.make_factory() binds named RecallAnalysisFn callbacks into a loss class with the same fitting interface. It compares observed and simulated summaries rather than assigning a likelihood to each recorded response. Recall Analyses shows the callback contract and uses the existing SPC calculation directly.
Its weights, scales and reduction determine how summary discrepancies contribute to the objective. Such a value is not NLL and cannot be put into an AIC formula. JAX-compatible simulation also does not by itself provide useful pathwise gradients through discrete recall samples.

title: Loss Functions
text:
Selecting observations
Ordinary losses receive the selected trial indices on every call. Row order and repeated indices are retained; selecting another participant does not change a previously supplied selection. Fitters call this same loss interface.
The ordinary interface is:
loss(trial_indices, base_params, free_param_names, candidates)
It returns one objective value per candidate column.
There is no preparation call before ordinary fitting. Gradient and evolutionary fitters pass trial indices to stable compiled functions; compatible shapes can reuse compilation while scoring different observations.


Evaluate the same candidates on the selected trials
loss(trial_indices, base_params, free_names, candidates)


Fitting Procedures explains how fitters consume these losses; the fitting template carries out a full run.
OptimizedCMR has a separate, experimental prepared-sequence implementation. Its acceleration is selected through explicit experimental fitting imports, described under Experimental OptimizedCMR. It adds no preparation requirements to ordinary losses or model factories.

title: Loss Functions
text:
Behavioral summaries and unordered recall
MemorySearchMseLoss calls the same dataset analyses on observations and simulations. One simulated dataset per candidate is shared across analyses. MemorySearchSpcMseLoss uses spc; MemorySearchCatSpcMseLoss stacks cat_spc results for explicit category values (defaults: field condition, values 1 and 2). Undefined observed bins are omitted. A missing prediction for an observed bin makes the fit invalid. Duplicate responses and repeated presentations follow those analyses’ definitions. Metadata and study-position recall codes stay aligned.
Simulation defaults are 20 repetitions for general/SPC MSE and 10 for category SPC, with seed zero. Both are configurable. Stopping remains active; responses after the observed response count are masked. This objective uses discrete simulation, so it is not a suitable pathwise-gradient loss.
Experimental RecallSetLikelihoodLoss sums over unordered item sequences and one final STOP. RecallPrefixLikelihoodLoss omits STOP. Both estimate the sum by sampling permutations and multiplying by the number of distinct orderings, including repeated-item multiplicities. The logarithm is also an approximation. Old permutation and MSE scores do not represent these corrected definitions.
See sequential scoring, behavioral MSE and permutation likelihood.

title: Model Evaluation
text:
On this page
  
    
    
    Which objects answer which questions?
    Fit-record conventions at the comparison boundary
    Compare summed negative log likelihoods
    Experimental cross-validation functionality
Evaluation uses datasets, parameter values and fit records already produced by the library. There is no single evaluation protocol: each comparison requires the representation and assumptions of the helper being used.

title: Model Evaluation
text:
Which objects answer which questions?



Question
Library inputs and operations
Complete procedure




Does the model reproduce a behavioral pattern?
Observed and simulated RecallDataset objects passed to the same analysis and plotting functions, such as plot_spc().
Simulation


What changes when a parameter changes?
Shared study inputs, a fixed model configuration and deliberate parameter interventions followed by simulation and analysis.
Parameter exploration


How do likelihood fits compare?
Compatible named fit records passed to comparison helpers in jaxcmr.summarize.
Model comparison



A behavioral match, an intervention and a likelihood comparison answer different questions. In particular, forced agreement with the observed recall length is not evidence that a model predicts when recall stops.

title: Model Evaluation
section: Fit-record conventions at the comparison boundary
text:
Fit-record conventions at the comparison boundary
FitResult provides parameter roles, objective values and row identifiers. Comparison helpers additionally use a name. The templates record the data selection, model configuration and objective needed to establish comparability.
Before comparing likelihood scores, establish that the records concern the same observations, included events and likelihood definition. Check whether parameters were pooled or independently fitted and how many values were estimated. A lower discrepancy loss cannot be substituted for NLL merely because both appear in a field named fitness.
The supplied source-only and broader eCMR records are pooled fits to the same all-condition selection with the same termination-excluded objective and stopping policy. Their emotional modulation differs in whether it also acts on temporal context. Each has ten free parameters and one pooled fit row.
Both supplied eCMR fits learn before context updating, fix emotional encoding drift at 1 and tie emotional recall drift to temporal recall drift. They omit the legacy emotion_drift_rate. Historical fits also require their original context equations and parameter interpretations; a shared import path alone does not identify that behavior.


0 — Locate the project inputs
from pathlib import Path

from jaxcmr.helpers import find_project_root, resolve_project_path

try:
    root_path = find_project_root()
except FileNotFoundError:
    root_path = Path.cwd()




Read the named pooled records and their comparison basis
from pathlib import Path
import json

files = {
    "Source-only eCMR": "Dupertuys2026_eCMR_source_only.json",
    "Broader eCMR": "Dupertuys2026_eCMR_broad.json",
}
records = [
    {**json.loads((Path(resolve_project_path("data/fits", root_path)) / filename).read_text()), "name": name}
    for name, filename in files.items()
]
for record in records:
    print(record["name"], "— fit IDs:", record["fits"]["subject"],
          "free parameters:", len(record["free"]))
print("Recorded trial selection:", records[0]["trial_query"])
print("Recorded loss:", records[0]["loss_function"])


Source-only eCMR — fit IDs: [-1] free parameters: 10
Broader eCMR — fit IDs: [-1] free parameters: 10
Recorded trial selection: data['list_type'] > 0
Recorded loss: jaxcmr.loss.transform_sequence_likelihood.ExcludeTerminationLikelihoodLoss

title: Model Evaluation
text:
Compare summed negative log likelihoods
jaxcmr.summarize.calculate_aic() accepts comparison records containing a model name, top-level integer subject IDs, free parameter names, and fitness. It returns a DataFrame sorted by AIC. Each fitness entry must be a summed negative log likelihood for one fitted parameter set:
\[\mathrm{AIC} = 2k + 2\,\mathrm{NLL}.\]
The saved fits already contain NLL. Select their scores and IDs explicitly and use list(record["free"]) to supply parameter names without optimizer bounds. Keep the original fit records for parameter summaries and simulation.
A pooled fit has subject=[-1] and incurs one parameter penalty. Independently fitted participant rows incur one penalty each. Supply unique integer IDs in subject, aligned with the scores and identifying the same set across models. Nested fits["subject"], plural subjects, omitted IDs, and string or floating-point IDs are not alternative comparison inputs. These are caller requirements; comparison functions do not normalize or validate those alternative forms.
For a custom table or plot, use the numerical operations directly. They return NumPy arrays without sorting, aggregation or fit-record metadata:
from jaxcmr.summarize import aic_scores, aicc_scores, bic_scores

# One summed NLL and one free-parameter count per pooled fit.
negative_log_likelihoods = [33.0, 30.0]
parameter_counts = [2, 1]
aic = aic_scores(negative_log_likelihoods, parameter_counts)  # [70, 62]
aicc = aicc_scores(negative_log_likelihoods, parameter_counts, 60)
bic = bic_scores(negative_log_likelihoods, parameter_counts, 60)
These operations use NumPy broadcasting. For a (models, participants) NLL matrix, give parameter counts shape (models, 1) and aligned observation counts shape (participants,). Each entry receives its own parameter penalty. The record-based functions below handle participant alignment and produce tables using these same calculations.


Prepare comparison records and calculate AIC
from jaxcmr.summarize import ModelComparison, calculate_aic

comparison_records: list[ModelComparison] = [
    {
        "name": record["name"],
        "subject": record["fits"]["subject"],
        "fitness": record["fitness"],
        "free": list(record["free"]),
    }
    for record in records
]
calculate_aic(comparison_records)









Model
AIC




1
Broader eCMR
14348.715746


0
Source-only eCMR
14358.852540







The supplied source-only and broader fits have NLLs 7169.426 and 7164.358, respectively. Their AIC difference is 10.137, favoring broader eCMR. The within-model differences between the two three-restart seed sets are 0.005 and 0.049 NLL units. The ranking is the same in both seed sets.
The result is a library-produced table. Lower AIC is preferred within this comparison; it does not establish a unique explanation of the experiment. Each model contributes one pooled parameter set, so len(free) is the parameter count for that row. calculate_aic_weights() uses the same NLL convention and parameter penalties as calculate_aic().
Participant-wise comparisons align rows by subject identifier and require finite scores for the same participant set. A pooled row is not a sample of independent participant estimates. Mean-difference helpers return the mean and interval half-width; median-difference helpers return the median and the actual bootstrap lower and upper endpoints.
calculate_bic_scores(results, n_obs) and the AICc helpers require positive observation counts for each fitted parameter row. Counts follow the first record’s original participant order; the library aligns them with the scores. Specify the scientific counting unit and selection explicitly. A scalar count is valid only for one fitted row; AICc requires each count to exceed k + 1.
floor_nested_fitness(comparison_records, nesting_pairs) returns separate comparison records and an adjustment table without changing the raw fits. Label adjusted scores and save the adjustment table beside them. Keep raw fits for parameter summaries, simulations and held-out evaluation: an adjusted score is not a newly optimized parameter set. The helper trusts the declared nesting relationships. Supply pairs of model names, such as [("CMR", "eCMR")]; two-element lists from JSON or YAML also work. Stringified Python expressions are not parsed.
bayesian_model_selection(comparison_records) aligns participant fits and uses the existing AIC/AICc-based log-evidence approximation, -IC / 2. It calls random_effects_model_selection(log_evidence, model_names), which also accepts log evidence obtained independently of these fit records:
from jaxcmr.summarize import random_effects_model_selection

# Supply your own log evidence: rows are the same participants in every column;
# columns are models in the order given by model_names.
selection = random_effects_model_selection(log_evidence, model_names)
The direct operation adds no parameter penalty and does not choose an evidence approximation. The caller establishes the evidence’s scientific interpretation and comparability. Both interfaces use the same population inference and return the same table columns. A pooled row cannot supply participant-level inference; failure to converge raises an error rather than returning a result.

title: Model Evaluation
text:
Experimental cross-validation functionality
jaxcmr.experimental.cross_validation contains an experimental driver, with CVResult describing fold-specific fits, participant identifiers, training scores and held-out scores. The current driver mixes pooled fitting with participant-level scoring and can return incorrect held-out scores; it is not ready for scientific use. A held-out comparison requires an appropriate split, fitting only the training observations and evaluating the held-out observations under the chosen objective. It is a different procedure from comparing in-sample AIC values.
For held-out comparisons, CVComparison uses the same top-level integer subject field and keeps held-out objectives in cv_fitness. Given an independently verified cv_result, the input is {"name": name, "subject": cv_result["subjects"], "cv_fitness": cv_result["cv_fitness"]}. This field selection does not resolve the experimental driver’s scientific limitations.
See Fitting Procedures for result structure and the model comparison template for the full pooled comparison. These interfaces organize the evidence; selecting a scientifically meaningful comparison remains part of the research design.

title: Model Components
text:
On this page
  
    
    
    Context, memory and response interfaces
    Creators supply components to a model
    What the model does with them
    Instance memory as an ordinary CMR component
Components provide the state representations and operations that a model combines. In CMR, item-to-context memory cues a context representation, context-to-item memory supports retrieval, and a response policy assigns probabilities to STOP and each item. The model determines when and how to use them.

title: Model Components
Model Components
section: Creators supply components to a model
text:
Creators supply components to a model
Models need fresh components with compatible dimensions and parameters. Creator functions provide these objects when a model is constructed.
Declaration from jaxcmr.typing:
class ContextCreateFn(Protocol):
    def __call__(self, item_count: int) -> Context: ...
Declaration from jaxcmr.typing:
class MemoryCreateFn(Protocol):
    def __call__(
        self,
        list_length: int,
        parameters: Parameters,
        context: Context,
    ) -> Memory: ...
Declaration from jaxcmr.typing:
class ResponsePolicyCreateFn[ModelT](Protocol):
    def __call__(
        self, list_length: int, parameters: Parameters
    ) -> ResponsePolicy[ModelT]: ...
Ordinary CMR’s make_factory() accepts four such callables:








Factory argument
Existing implementation used here
Role




context_create_fn
context.init
Construct temporal context.


mfc_create_fn
linear_memory.init_mfc
Construct item-to-context memory.


mcf_create_fn
linear_memory.init_mcf
Construct context-to-item memory.


response_policy_create_fn
RecallUntilExhausted
Assign probabilities to STOP and each item.



A compatible function or callable class can occupy one of these arguments. Each memory creator returns one memory with the appropriate direction and dimensions. Changing a creator changes that component’s implementation; the model still owns its event ordering, parameter interpretation and composition rules. Other models may expose different configuration choices.


0 — Locate the project inputs
from pathlib import Path

from jaxcmr.helpers import find_project_root, resolve_project_path

try:
    root_path = find_project_root()
except FileNotFoundError:
    root_path = Path.cwd()




Connect the component creators and inspect the resulting objects
from pathlib import Path
import json
import jax
import jax.numpy as jnp
from jaxcmr.helpers import load_data
from jaxcmr.dataset import generate_trial_mask
from jaxcmr.components import context, linear_memory
from jaxcmr.components.response import RecallUntilExhausted
from jaxcmr.models.cmr import make_factory

jax.config.update("jax_enable_x64", True)
data = load_data(resolve_project_path("data/Dupertuys2026.h5", root_path))
record = json.loads(Path(resolve_project_path("data/fits/Dupertuys2026_CMR_demo.json", root_path)).read_text())
parameters = {name: values[0] for name, values in record["fits"].items()
              if name != "subject"}
for name in ("allow_repeated_recalls", "learn_after_context_update"):
    parameters[name] = bool(parameters[name])

CMRFactory = make_factory(
    mfc_create_fn=linear_memory.init_mfc,
    mcf_create_fn=linear_memory.init_mcf,
    context_create_fn=context.init,
    response_policy_create_fn=RecallUntilExhausted,
)

factory = CMRFactory(data, features=None)
mixed = generate_trial_mask(data, "data['list_type'] == 1")
trial_index = int(jnp.flatnonzero(mixed)[0])
initial = factory.create_trial_model(trial_index, parameters)
print("Context:", type(initial.context).__name__, initial.context.state.shape)
print("Item-to-context memory:", type(initial.mfc).__name__, initial.mfc.state.shape)
print("Context-to-item memory:", type(initial.mcf).__name__, initial.mcf.state.shape)
print("Response:", type(initial.response_policy).__name__)

Item-to-context memory: LinearMemory (12, 13)
Context-to-item memory: LinearMemory (13, 12)
Response: RecallUntilExhausted

title: Model Components
section: What the model does with them
text:
What the model does with them
For a CMR study event, item-to-context memory is probed with the item pattern. Context integrates that input using encoding drift. The model then updates both associative memories; learn_after_context_update determines which context state is used for learning. During retrieval, context-to-item memory supplies one evidence value per item. Here the response policy RecallUntilExhausted assigns all probability to available items, weighting their relative evidence by choice_sensitivity. It assigns all probability to STOP once the items are exhausted.


Display the context after CMR processes one study event
from IPython.display import display

updated = initial.experience(data["pres_itemnos"][trial_index, 0])
print("Original study count:", int(initial.study_index))
print("Updated study count:", int(updated.study_index))
print("Context changed:", not bool(jnp.allclose(
    initial.context.state, updated.context.state
)))
display(updated.context)


Original study count: 0
Updated study count: 1
Context changed: True





The figure uses the context object’s built-in notebook display. It shows the representation after one update; the original model retains its earlier state. A compatible replacement must satisfy the required dimensions, functional update behavior and JAX operations, as well as the protocol’s named methods. A response policy additionally needs the attributes of the model or view passed to it.
See Memory Search Models for the enclosing lifecycle and the parameter exploration template for changing parameters within a fixed model configuration.

title: Model Components
section: Instance memory as an ordinary CMR component
text:
Instance memory as an ordinary CMR component
The instance-memory creators can replace the linear-memory creators above. They store each learned association in a separate row instead of adding it to a shared association matrix. The model still controls study, recall and stopping; this does not use the unfinished experimental.instance_cmr model.
from jaxcmr.components import instance_memory

InstanceMemoryCMR = make_factory(
    mfc_create_fn=instance_memory.init_mfc,
    mcf_create_fn=instance_memory.init_mcf,
    context_create_fn=context.init,
    response_policy_create_fn=RecallUntilExhausted,
)
instance_parameters = parameters | {
    "mfc_trace_sensitivity": 1.0,
    "mcf_trace_sensitivity": 1.0,
}
instance_model = InstanceMemoryCMR(data, features=None).create_trial_model(
    trial_index, instance_parameters
)
A trace contains its input pattern followed by its output pattern multiplied by the learning rate. Probing computes the cue’s dot product with each stored input, divides those supports by their positive maximum, raises them to the trace sensitivity, and sums the correspondingly weighted outputs. Unsupported traces contribute zero. Sensitivity one uses the same normalization; higher sensitivities favor better-matching traces more strongly. This differs from older versions, which skipped normalization at exactly one.
probe_without_scale(cue) bypasses normalization and the sensitivity power. It returns the result of probing the summed outer-product association matrix represented by the traces. probe(cue) can differ in magnitude even at sensitivity one. Trace sensitivity is separate from CMR’s choice_sensitivity, which acts on item support after the memory probe.
Both creators reserve space for list_length new study associations in addition to the initial associations. Clients supplying their own traces provide sufficient capacity, zero unused rows, nonnegative finite cue supports and positive sensitivity. Memory state layouts differ: use the common probe/associate operations unless you specifically need the stored traces.

This guide explains JAXCMR’s data structures, interfaces and conventions: what each part receives, what it returns and where another part uses it. It also identifies entry points for supplying compatible functions or implementations. The Templates assemble these parts into complete research procedures.

title: Library Guide
text:
How the interfaces connect






flowchart TB
    D["RecallDataset"] --> F["MemorySearchModelFactory"]
    F --> M["MemorySearch"]
    C["Context · Memory · TerminationPolicy"] --> M
    D --> L["LossFn"]
    M -->|event probabilities| L
    M --> S["TrialSimulator"]
    S --> SD["Simulated RecallDataset"]
    D --> A["Recall analyses"]
    SD --> A
    A -. "RecallAnalysisFn callback" .-> L
    L --> O["FittingAlgorithm"]
    O --> R["FitResult"]
    R -->|assigned parameters| S
    R --> E["Evaluation helpers"]
    A --> E






A model factory creates a model for an experiment and parameter values. Likelihood calculations follow recorded responses through that model; simulation samples new responses. Both observed and simulated datasets can enter recall analyses. A compatible analysis callback can also supply the summary used by a behavioral objective. Fitters search parameter values using a loss and return records for subsequent simulation and evaluation.
Simulation can use hand-chosen parameters without a fit. Analysis can describe observations without a model. These are connected interfaces, not a mandatory sequence of steps.

title: Library Guide
text:
What a protocol provides
A Python Protocol describes the attributes and methods a consumer expects. A compatible implementation need not inherit from that protocol. For a callable protocol such as RecallAnalysisFn, an ordinary function with the specified arguments and behavior can be passed directly to its consumer. The analysis callback example shows this connection using an existing SPC calculation.
Signatures alone are not enough: array dimensions, item coding, parameter order and JAX-compatible operations also determine whether implementations work together. Each topic explains these responsibilities alongside the relevant declaration. Examples illustrate one connection at a time.
RecallDataset and FitResult are dictionary types, not protocols. They describe fields and alignment, without being comprehensive runtime validators. Other conventions, such as template-added provenance or objective signs expected by comparison helpers, are established by the procedures that produce and consume the records.

title: Library Guide
text:
Configuring a reusable procedure
Template notebooks separate literal settings from the Python objects constructed from them:

A tagged parameters cell holds paths, selections, parameter values, import names and output locations. Parameterized execution can replace these literals for another run.
Setup imports implementations and constructs factories, masks and other derived objects from those settings.
The procedure produces outputs and retains the effective settings.

Independent executions need separate output locations. Changes to fit parameters or simulation settings require corresponding new simulation outputs. The Templates explain parameterized execution and provide complete procedures; this guide describes the structures they connect.

title: Library Guide
text:
Using the illustrations
The topic notebooks retain small executed examples using the existing war-photo-recall observations and supplied fits. Their protocol declarations are visible; expand a labeled code block to inspect an executable example. To rerun one, use Download notebook and place it beside the shared data/ folder from the Templates downloads. The homepage gives the installation command.

title: From data to model comparison
text:
On this page
  
    
    
    Describe observed recall
    Inspect a fitted model
    Generate responses from the fits
    Compare observed and simulated recall

    Sequence the templates with Papermill
Follow the war-photo-recall data through analysis, fitting, simulation and comparison. The first sections identify the settings and outputs in each template; the final section executes the same sequence with Papermill, including a separate fitting run for each model. It reuses the supplied completed fits by default.
Use the repository and environment from Local setup with VS Code. Open this notebook in that environment. The repository contains the observations and completed fits; no lab-drive files are needed. For preparing your own inputs, start with Preparing data for JAXCMR.
1 — Configure the tutorial work units
project_root = None  # The JAXCMR checkout; set explicitly when working elsewhere.
output_dir = "results/tutorial/model-comparison"
data_path = "data/Dupertuys2026.h5"

fit_sources = {
    "CMR": "data/fits/Dupertuys2026_CMR_demo.json",

}
model_labels = {
    "CMR": "CMR",
    "eCMR_source_only": "Source-only eCMR",
    "eCMR_broad": "Broader eCMR",
}
redo_fits = False  # True launches the full recorded optimization settings.
experiment_count = 10
simulation_seed = 1
